research: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat_raffle — UK meat raffles are a pub social ritual, ~£1 tickets, prizes from a local butcher: so the prize reads as cling-filmed cuts on a plain tray with a butcher's paper bag, no branding
https://heptonstall.org/tag/meat/ — real British locals still run weekly meat raffles; it is ordinary, not quaint

https://www.morningadvertiser.co.uk/Article/2023/07/04/Stonegate-and-Heineken-UK-promoting-inclusivity-in-pubs — Stonegate/Heineken research: ethnic minority customers are regulars where a pub feels inclusive; the local should look like its town, so every person in frame gets a specific ordinary look rather than 'diverse crowd'

https://thehobbledehoy.com/2021/02/19/you-know-you-dont-belong-why-people-of-colour-dont-feel-welcome-in-pubs/ — the failure mode is people of colour as tokens at the edge; so put them at the centre of the receiving table and give them the reaction

https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — with a reference attached, spend the prompt on action, layout and mood, not on the referenced identity
https://openart.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-lite-prompt-guide/ — quote exact text and say where it sits; keep it short; so one number, in quotes, on one sheet facing the camera
notes: Beat 5, the prize. Option a is the handover itself, close and warm, with no number in frame (the receiving table carries the diversity note and the reaction). Option b is the exit, shot from inside: the receiving table in the foreground, Bob a silhouette in the open doorway against teal rain, his abandoned sheet reading 300,000 facing the camera as the only legible number. Both: no brands, Bob described only by position, action, posture, expression.
